import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ropelength problems

The *ropelength* of a curve $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(L)/\tau(L)$, the
quotient of its length by its *thickness* $\tau(L)$, the radius of the largest embedded normal
tube around $L$. Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, the thickness is the
infimum of the circumradius $r(x, y, z)$ over all triples of distinct points of $L$. The
ropelength of a knot or link type is the infimum of the ropelengths of its representatives.
Curves of positive thickness are $C^{1,1}$, so this infimum ranges over $C^{1,1}$ representatives;
it is attained, and the minimizers are called *tight* or *ideal*.

Units: thickness is a radius, so a tight link has an embedded normal tube of unit radius and its
ropelength equals its length. With this convention the Hopf link has ropelength $8\pi$. This is the
convention of Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan and of the Wikipedia article.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [CKS02] J. Cantarella, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and
  links*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002), 257–286. [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- [CFKSW06] J. Cantarella, J. H. G. Fu, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, N. C. Wrinkle, *Criticality
  for the Gehring link problem*, Geom. Topol. 10 (2006), 2055–2116.
  [arXiv:math/0402212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402212)
- [DEPZ19] Y. Diao, C. Ernst, A. Por, U. Ziegler, *The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in
  terms of their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019), 1950085.
-/

open MeasureTheory Topology

open scoped EuclideanGeometry ENNReal unitInterval

namespace RopelengthProblems

/-- A subset `K ⊆ ℝ³` is a *knot* if it is the image of a topological embedding of the circle. -/
def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ ∧ Set.range γ = K

/-- Two subsets `A`, `B` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family
`H t : ℝ³ → ℝ³`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' A = B`.
The knot (or link) type of `A` is its ambient isotopy class. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : C(I × ℝ³, ℝ³), (∀ t, IsHomeomorph fun x => H (t, x)) ∧ (∀ x, H (0, x) = x) ∧
    (fun x => H (1, x)) '' A = B

/-- Every set is ambient isotopic to itself, via the constant isotopy. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem ambientIsotopic_refl (A : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨⟨fun p => p.2, continuous_snd⟩, fun _ => IsHomeomorph.id, fun _ => rfl, Set.image_id' A⟩

/-- The standard unknot: the unit circle in the coordinate plane `x₂ = 0`. -/
def unknot : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x | x 0 ^ 2 + x 1 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ x 2 = 0}

/-- The standard **Borromean rings**: three mutually perpendicular ellipses, one in each
coordinate plane, with semi-axes `2` and `1`. The major axis of the ellipse in the plane
`x₂ = 0` lies along the `x₀`-axis, that of the ellipse in the plane `x₀ = 0` along the `x₁`-axis,
and that of the ellipse in the plane `x₁ = 0` along the `x₂`-axis. The three curves are pairwise
disjoint, and each passes through the disc spanned by the next one but not through the disc spanned
by the previous one. This is the classical realization of the Borromean rings by three mutually
perpendicular ellipses (or golden rectangles). -/
def borromeanRings : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x | x 0 ^ 2 / 4 + x 1 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ x 2 = 0} ∪
    {x | x 1 ^ 2 / 4 + x 2 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ x 0 = 0} ∪
    {x | x 2 ^ 2 / 4 + x 0 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ x 1 = 0}

/-- The *thickness* `τ(L)` of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³` (Gonzalez–Maddocks, [CKS02, §1]): the infimum of the
circumradius `r(x, y, z)` over all triples of distinct points `x, y, z ∈ L`, where collinear
triples have `r = ∞` and are therefore omitted. For a `C¹` link this is the radius of the largest
embedded normal tube around `L`, and a link of positive thickness is `C^{1,1}` [CKS02, §1–2]. -/
noncomputable def thickness (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2) (_ : ∀ i, s.points i ∈ L), ENNReal.ofReal s.circumradius

/-- The *ropelength* `Len(L) / τ(L)` of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³`, where the length `Len(L)` is the
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of `L` (for a link, the total length of its components).
It is `∞` when `L` has thickness zero or infinite length. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] L / thickness L

/-- The ropelength of the knot or link type of `K`: the infimum of the ropelengths of all sets
ambient isotopic to `K`. By [CKS02, §2] the infimum is attained when the type is tame. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (L : Set ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K L), ropelength L

/-- A knot or link type is *tame* if it has a representative of positive thickness. A curve of
positive thickness is `C^{1,1}` and hence tame in the classical sense, and conversely a polygonal
knot is ambient isotopic to a smooth one, which has positive thickness. -/
def IsTame (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ L, AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ 0 < thickness L

/-- The *crossings* of the projection of `L ⊆ ℝ³` along a direction `v`: the unordered pairs of
distinct points of `L` that project to the same point of a plane transverse to `v`. -/
def crossings (L : Set ℝ³) (v : ℝ³) : Set (Sym2 ℝ³) :=
  {p | ∃ x ∈ L, ∃ y ∈ L, p = s(x, y) ∧ x ≠ y ∧ ∃ t : ℝ, y = x + t • v}

/-- The *crossing number* `Cr(K)` of the knot or link type of `K`: the least number of crossings
in a projection of a representative of the type, where the infimum runs over all representatives
and all projection directions. A projection with finitely many crossings can be perturbed to a
regular diagram with at most as many crossings, so for tame types this is the classical crossing
number: the least number of crossings in a diagram of the type. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (L : Set ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K L) (v : ℝ³) (_ : v ≠ 0), (crossings L v).encard

/-- The unknot has crossing number `0`: its standard representative projects injectively along
the `x₂`-axis. -/
@[category test, AMS 57]
theorem crossingNumber_unknot : crossingNumber unknot = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ bot_le
  refine (iInf₂_le unknot (ambientIsotopic_refl _)).trans ?_
  refine (iInf₂_le (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1) (by simp)).trans ?_
  suffices crossings unknot (EuclideanSpace.single 2 1) = ∅ by simp [this]
  ext p
  simp only [crossings, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_exists, not_and]
  rintro x ⟨-, hx⟩ y ⟨-, hy⟩ rfl hxy t ht
  apply hxy
  have : t = 0 := by
    have := congrArg (fun z : ℝ³ => z 2) ht
    simpa [hx, hy] using this.symm
  simp [ht, this]

/-- For every knot $K$, $L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$ [DEPZ19],
and there are knot families with $L(K)$ proportional to $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$. No knot family
with super-linear dependence of ropelength on crossing number has been observed, and it is
conjectured that the tight upper bound is linear: there is a constant $c > 0$ such that
$L(K) \le c \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ for every nontrivial tame knot $K$. The unknot is excluded
since it has crossing number $0$ but positive ropelength. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : Set ℝ³, IsKnot K → IsTame K → ¬ AmbientIsotopic K unknot →
      minRopelength K ≤ ENNReal.ofReal c * (crossingNumber K : ℝ≥0∞) := by
  sorry

/-- The ropelength of the Borromean rings is conjectured to be $58.006$ (to three decimal
places): the guitar-shaped critical configuration of Cantarella, Fu, Kusner, Sullivan and Wrinkle
[CFKSW06], built from parameterized arcs, has ropelength approximately $58.0060$ and is conjectured
to be the ropelength minimizer. Ropelength is measured with unit-radius thickness, so that the Hopf
link has ropelength $8\pi$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.ii :
    ∃ r : ℝ, |r - 58.006| ≤ 0.0005 ∧ minRopelength borromeanRings = ENNReal.ofReal r := by
  sorry

end RopelengthProblems

modeling_decisions: Knots/links are modelled as subsets of ℝ³ (images of embeddings), and knot types as ambient isotopy classes of sets (unoriented types). Ropelength and crossing number are invariant under orientation reversal and mirror image, so this loses nothing.

Thickness follows Gonzalez–Maddocks/CKS (infimal circumradius over distinct triples) rather than Federer's reach or the normal injectivity radius; CKS prove these agree for C¹ links and that positive thickness forces C^{1,1}. Consequently the infimum over all (even wild) representatives equals the infimum over C^{1,1} representatives, as in the literature.

Length is taken to be the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the set (Mathlib normalization gives μH[1](segment) = its length), which equals arc length for simple rectifiable curves and sums over link components; ropelength is ℝ≥0∞-valued so that thickness zero or infinite length gives ropelength ∞ (CKS: wild links have infinite ropelength). No real division-by-zero junk arises.

Crossing number is defined as an infimum over all representatives and all projection directions of the number of unordered double-point pairs of the projection (ℕ∞-valued). Regular diagrams are included (giving ≤ the classical crossing number), and any projection with finitely many double pairs can be perturbed, within the knot type, to a regular diagram with at most that many crossings (a k-fold point contributes C(k,2) pairs and perturbs to ≤ C(k,2) transverse crossings, tangential double points contribute 1 and can be removed), so the definition agrees with the classical crossing number for tame types. Test `crossingNumber_unknot` confirms Cr(unknot) = 0.

Slot (i): the unknot is excluded via ¬ AmbientIsotopic K unknot (Cr = 0 but ropelength > 0); the O-statement is stated as ∃ c > 0, ∀ nontrivial tame knot K, minRopelength K ≤ ofReal c * Cr(K). Since Cr ≥ 3 for nontrivial knots this is equivalent to allowing an additive constant. The tameness hypothesis (IsTame: some representative of positive thickness, equivalent to classical tameness) restricts to the knots the conjecture is about; for wild knots both sides would be ∞ anyway.

Slot (ii): the rounded figure 58.006 is read as 'equal to 58.006 to three decimal places', i.e. ∃ r, |r − 58.006| ≤ 0.0005 ∧ minRopelength borromeanRings = ENNReal.ofReal r. The CFKSW configuration has ropelength ≈ 58.0060, which lies in this interval (and also in the alternative reading [58.006, 58.007) suggested in the notes). Unit-radius thickness convention (Hopf link = 8π) as in CKS and Wikipedia.

The Borromean rings are represented by the concrete set of three mutually perpendicular ellipses x₀²/4 + x₁² = 1 (x₂ = 0), x₁²/4 + x₂² = 1 (x₀ = 0), x₂²/4 + x₀² = 1 (x₁ = 0): pairwise disjoint, each pair geometrically unlinked, each ellipse threading the disc of the next one — the classical ellipse/golden-rectangle realization (isotopic to the icosahedral golden-rectangle configuration by scaling the axes). A reviewer should check this reference configuration.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ropelength problems

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Cantarella, Kusner, and Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
-/

namespace RopelengthProblems

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal


/-- Three-dimensional Euclidean space. -/
abbrev Euclidean3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- An `n`-component link is an embedded disjoint union of `n` circles in Euclidean space. -/
structure Link (n : ℕ) where
  toFun : Fin n × AddCircle (1 : ℝ) → Euclidean3
  isEmbedding : Topology.IsEmbedding toFun

instance {n : ℕ} : FunLike (Link n) (Fin n × AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) Euclidean3 where
  coe := Link.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun L K h ↦ by
    cases L with
    | mk f hf =>
      cases K with
      | mk g hg =>
        dsimp only [Link.toFun] at h
        subst g
        rfl

/-- Two links have the same link type when an ambient isotopy carries one image to the other. -/
def AmbientIsotopic {n : ℕ} (L K : Link n) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : ℝ → Euclidean3 ≃ₜ Euclidean3,
    ContinuousOn (fun p : ℝ × Euclidean3 ↦ H p.1 p.2) (Icc 0 1 ×ˢ (univ : Set Euclidean3)) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl Euclidean3 ∧
    H 1 '' range L = range K

/-- The radius of the circle through three points, or infinity when there is no such circle. -/
noncomputable def circumradius (x y z : Euclidean3) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sInf ({r : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ c : Euclidean3, edist c x = r ∧ edist c y = r ∧ edist c z = r} :
    Set ℝ≥0∞)

/--
The thickness of a link is the infimum of the circumradii of triples of distinct points on it.
This is the three-point characterization of the radius of the largest embedded normal tube.
-/
noncomputable def thickness {n : ℕ} (L : Link n) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sInf ({r : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ x ∈ range L, ∃ y ∈ range L, ∃ z ∈ range L,
    x ≠ y ∧ y ≠ z ∧ z ≠ x ∧ r = circumradius x y z} : Set ℝ≥0∞)

/-- The total length of a link, measured by one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. -/
noncomputable def length {n : ℕ} (L : Link n) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  Measure.hausdorffMeasure 1 (range L)

/-- The ropelength of a link type is the infimum of length divided by thickness in that type. -/
noncomputable def ropelength {n : ℕ} (L : Link n) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sInf ({r : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ K : Link n, AmbientIsotopic L K ∧
    r = length K / thickness K} : Set ℝ≥0∞)

/-- Projection of three-dimensional Euclidean space onto its first two coordinates. -/
def planarProjection (x : Euclidean3) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 fun i ↦ x (Fin.castLE (by decide) i)

/-- Ordered pairs of distinct points of a knot that have the same planar projection. -/
def doublePointPairs (K : Link 1) : Set
    ((Fin 1 × AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) × (Fin 1 × AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) :=
  {p | p.1 ≠ p.2 ∧ planarProjection (K p.1) = planarProjection (K p.2)}

/--
The crossing number of a knot is the least number of double points in a finite planar projection
of an ambient-isotopic representative. Ordered pairs are divided by two.
-/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Link 1) : ℕ :=
  sInf ({m : ℕ | ∃ L : Link 1, AmbientIsotopic K L ∧
    (doublePointPairs L).Finite ∧ m = (doublePointPairs L).ncard / 2} : Set ℕ)

/--
There is a universal positive finite constant $c$ such that every nontrivial tame knot $K$
satisfies
$$
  \operatorname{Ropelength}(K) \le c\,\operatorname{Cr}(K).
$$
Thus the conjectured tight upper bound for ropelength in terms of crossing number is linear.
The condition $0 < \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ excludes the unknot.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ≥0, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : Link 1, 0 < crossingNumber K →
      ropelength K ≤ (c : ℝ≥0∞) * crossingNumber K := by
  sorry

end RopelengthProblems
modeling_decisions: Represented an n-component link as a topological embedding of a disjoint union of n copies of the additive unit circle into three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Defined link type by ambient isotopy, represented as a continuous family of ambient homeomorphisms on the unit time interval; endpoint equality is imposed on unparameterized images, allowing component permutation and reparameterization.
Used one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the embedded image for total link length. For a disjoint finite union of rectifiable embedded curves this is the sum of component lengths.

Used the Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan three-point characterization of thickness: the infimum of circumradii over triples of distinct image points. Circumradius is the least common distance to an equidistant center; this is infinity for three distinct collinear points.

Defined ropelength as the infimum of total length divided by thickness over ambient-isotopic representatives. Although the structure permits arbitrary topological embeddings, representatives with positive three-point thickness have the required C^{1,1} geometric regularity; zero-thickness nondegenerate representatives do not lower the quotient.

Defined crossing number directly as the minimum finite number of projection double points among ambient-isotopic representatives. Ordered pairs of distinct preimages are divided by two. Fixing projection to the first two coordinates is harmless because representatives vary by ambient isotopy.

Quantified the linear-bound constant in ℝ≥0, so it is finite, and required it to be positive. Restricted to knots with positive crossing number, exactly the intended exclusion of the unknot; finite-projection representatives are tame.
Omitted the Borromean-rings slot rather than using the non-characterizing condition that every two-component sublink is trivial or introducing a semantically empty named link type.

open Topology

namespace RopelengthProblems

abbrev E2 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)
abbrev E3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
abbrev ParameterDisk := Metric.closedBall (0 : ℂ) 1
abbrev ParameterCircle := {z : ParameterDisk | ‖(z : ℂ)‖ = 1}
abbrev Time := Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- A geometric knot is a topological embedding of a circle in Euclidean three-space. -/
structure KnotEmbedding where
  toFun : Circle → E3
  isEmbedding : IsEmbedding toFun

instance : CoeFun KnotEmbedding fun _ ↦ Circle → E3 := ⟨KnotEmbedding.toFun⟩

/-- Two geometric knots are ambient isotopic if a continuous path of homeomorphisms of
three-space, starting at the identity, carries the image of one knot onto the other. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K L : KnotEmbedding) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Time → (E3 ≃ₜ E3),
    Continuous (fun p : Time × E3 ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H ⟨0, by norm_num⟩ = Homeomorph.refl E3 ∧
    H ⟨1, by norm_num⟩ '' Set.range K = Set.range L

/-- An embedded knot is the unknot if its image bounds a topologically embedded disk. -/
def IsUnknot (K : KnotEmbedding) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : ParameterDisk → E3, IsEmbedding F ∧ F '' Set.range ((↑) : ParameterCircle → ParameterDisk) =
    Set.range K

/-- The denominator in the metric formula for the circumradius of three points. -/
def circumradiusDenominator (x y z : E3) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt ((dist x y + dist y z + dist z x) *
    (-dist x y + dist y z + dist z x) *
    (dist x y - dist y z + dist z x) *
    (dist x y + dist y z - dist z x))

/-- The radius of the circle through three noncollinear points, expressed by Heron's formula. -/
def circumradius (x y z : E3) : ℝ :=
  dist x y * dist y z * dist z x / circumradiusDenominator x y z

/-- The thickness of a set in three-space is the infimum of the circumradii of triples of
distinct, noncollinear points in the set. -/
def thickness (S : Set E3) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ x ∈ S, ∃ y ∈ S, ∃ z ∈ S,
    x ≠ y ∧ y ≠ z ∧ z ≠ x ∧ 0 < circumradiusDenominator x y z ∧
    r = circumradius x y z}

/-- The length of a geometric knot is the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of its image. -/
def knotLength (K : KnotEmbedding) : ℝ :=
  (MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure 1 (Set.range K)).toReal

/-- A representative is admissible for ropelength when it has positive thickness and finite
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. These conditions force the usual `C¹,¹` regularity. -/
def IsRopeRepresentative (K : KnotEmbedding) : Prop :=
  0 < thickness (Set.range K) ∧
    MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure 1 (Set.range K) ≠ ⊤

/-- A knot is tame if its ambient-isotopy class has an admissible ropelength representative. -/
def IsTame (K : KnotEmbedding) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : KnotEmbedding, AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ IsRopeRepresentative L

/-- The ropelength of a tame knot type is the infimum of length divided by thickness over its
admissible representatives. -/
def ropelength (K : KnotEmbedding) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ L : KnotEmbedding, AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ IsRopeRepresentative L ∧
    r = knotLength L / thickness (Set.range L)}

/-- The ordered pairs of distinct parameters identified by a planar linear projection. -/
def projectedDoublePairs (K : KnotEmbedding) (P : E3 →L[ℝ] E2) : Set (Circle × Circle) :=
  {p | p.1 ≠ p.2 ∧ P (K p.1) = P (K p.2)}


/-- A projection is regular when its double-pair set is finite and its cardinality is stable under
small surjective linear perturbations. This excludes tangencies and other projections at which
Reidemeister transitions change the crossing count. -/
def IsRegularProjection (K : KnotEmbedding) (P : E3 →L[ℝ] E2) : Prop :=
  (projectedDoublePairs K P).encard ≠ ⊤ ∧
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ Q : E3 →L[ℝ] E2, dist Q P < ε → Function.Surjective Q →
      (projectedDoublePairs K Q).encard = (projectedDoublePairs K P).encard

/-- The crossing number of a knot type is the least number of double points in a finite planar
linear projection of an ambient-isotopic representative. Ordered preimage pairs are counted, so
their cardinality is twice the number of crossings. -/
def crossingNumber (K : KnotEmbedding) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ L : KnotEmbedding, ∃ P : E3 →L[ℝ] E2,
    AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ IsRopeRepresentative L ∧ Function.Surjective P ∧
    IsRegularProjection L P ∧ (projectedDoublePairs L P).encard = 2 * n}

/-- It is conjectured that the tight asymptotic upper bound for ropelength in terms of crossing
number is linear: there is a universal constant $c>0$ such that every nontrivial tame knot $K$
satisfies $\operatorname{Rop}(K) \le c\,\operatorname{Cr}(K)$. The unknot is excluded because its
crossing number is zero but its ropelength is positive. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : KnotEmbedding, IsTame K → ¬ IsUnknot K →
      ropelength K ≤ c * crossingNumber K := by

end RopelengthProblems
modeling_decisions: A geometric knot is modeled as a topological embedding of Mathlib's `Circle` into Euclidean three-space; knot type is handled by an explicit ambient-isotopy relation given by a jointly continuous path of ambient homeomorphisms starting at the identity.
The unknot is characterized as an embedded circle whose image is the boundary of a topologically embedded disk. It is explicitly excluded, as required because its crossing number is zero.
Tameness is stated explicitly. A knot is called tame when its ambient-isotopy class contains a positive-thickness representative of finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

Curve length is one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Thickness is the Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan/Gonzalez–Maddocks infimum of circumradii over triples of distinct noncollinear image points, using Heron's metric formula. The ropelength invariant is the infimum of length/thickness over ambient-isotopic finite-length, positive-thickness representatives; these hypotheses give the intended C^{1,1} geometric class and avoid the `ENNReal.toReal ∞ = 0` boundary case.

Crossing number is modeled as the least finite double-point count among surjective planar linear projections of admissible ambient-isotopic representatives. Ordered preimage pairs are counted and equated to twice the crossing count. Local stability under small surjective linear perturbations is required to exclude tangential projections at Reidemeister transitions and capture regular diagram crossings.

The source says the tight upper bound 'should be linear', interpreted per the decomposition notes as a single universal c > 0 satisfying ropelength(K) ≤ c * Cr(K) for every nontrivial tame knot, rather than merely a statement about one observed family.

Slot ii was not weakened to an arbitrary three-component Brunnian link: that would include isotopy classes other than the Borromean rings. It was therefore omitted rather than assigning 58.006 to a subtly broader class.

/-!
# Ropelength problems

The *ropelength* of a knot or link $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is the quotient
$\operatorname{Len}(L) / \tau(L)$ of its length by its *thickness*, the radius of the largest
embedded normal tube around $L$. Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, the
thickness is the infimum, over all triples of distinct points of $L$, of the radius of the circle
through the three points; it is positive exactly when $L$ is an embedded $C^{1,1}$ curve. The
ropelength of a knot (or link) *type* is the infimum of the ropelength over all curves of that type
(a minimizer always exists for tame types). Thickness is measured as a radius, so the tight Hopf
link has ropelength $8\pi$.

This file states two open problems about ropelength listed on Wikipedia:

* the ropelength of a knot is conjectured to be bounded by a constant times its crossing number;
* the minimal ropelength of the Borromean rings is conjectured to be $58.006$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* J. Cantarella, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*,
  Invent. Math. 150 (2002), [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
* J. Cantarella, J. H. G. Fu, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, N. C. Wrinkle, *Criticality for the
  Gehring link problem*, Geom. Topol. 10 (2006), [arXiv:math/0402212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402212)
* Y. Diao, C. Ernst, A. Por, U. Ziegler, *The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in terms of
  their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019),
  [doi:10.1142/S0218216519500858](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218216519500858)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry ENNReal NNReal
open MeasureTheory

namespace RopelengthProblems

/-- A subset `K` of `ℝ³` is a *knot* if it is homeomorphic to a circle. -/
def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Circle ≃ₜ K)

/-- Two subsets `A`, `B` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' A = B`.
Knot and link types are the equivalence classes of this relation. -/
def IsAmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : unitInterval → ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' A = B

/-- Ambient isotopy is reflexive. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem IsAmbientIsotopic.refl (A : Set ℝ³) : IsAmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id A⟩

/-- The round unit circle in the plane `x₂ = 0`, representing the trivial knot. -/
def unknot : Set ℝ³ :=
  {p | p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ p 2 = 0}

/-- A standard realization of the *Borromean rings*: three ellipses with semi-axes `1` and `2`,
lying in the three coordinate planes, with the major axis of each ellipse along a different
coordinate axis (the ellipse in the plane `x₀ = 0` has its major axis along the `x₂`-axis, the one
in `x₁ = 0` along the `x₀`-axis and the one in `x₂ = 0` along the `x₁`-axis). Replacing each
ellipse by the rectangle with the same axes, and rescaling the major axes to the golden ratio,
gives the three mutually perpendicular golden rectangles inside a regular icosahedron. -/
def borromeanRings : Set ℝ³ :=
  {p | p 0 = 0 ∧ p 1 ^ 2 + p 2 ^ 2 / 4 = 1} ∪
    {p | p 1 = 0 ∧ p 2 ^ 2 + p 0 ^ 2 / 4 = 1} ∪
    {p | p 2 = 0 ∧ p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 / 4 = 1}

open scoped Classical in
/-- The radius of the circle through three points `x`, `y`, `z` of `ℝ³`, as an extended
nonnegative real. It is `⊤` when the points are collinear (or not pairwise distinct). -/
noncomputable def circumradius (x y z : ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  if h : AffineIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z] then
    ENNReal.ofReal (Affine.Simplex.mk ![x, y, z] h).circumradius
  else ⊤

/-- Triples with a repeated point have infinite circumradius. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem circumradius_self_left (x z : ℝ³) : circumradius x x z = ⊤ := by
  rw [circumradius, dif_neg]
  intro h
  exact absurd (h.injective.ne (show (0 : Fin 3) ≠ 1 by decide)) (by simp)

/-- The *thickness* of a subset `L` of `ℝ³` (Gonzalez–Maddocks, Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan): the
infimum of the circumradii of all triples of distinct points of `L`. For a link `L` this is the
radius of the largest embedded normal tube around `L`; it is positive exactly when `L` is an
embedded $C^{1,1}$ curve. -/
noncomputable def thickness (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (x ∈ L) (y ∈ L) (z ∈ L) (_ : x ≠ y) (_ : x ≠ z) (_ : y ≠ z), circumradius x y z

/-- The *ropelength* of a subset `L` of `ℝ³`: its length (the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of
`L`, which for a link is the sum of the lengths of its components) divided by its thickness.
A knot or link of thickness `0` (one that is not $C^{1,1}$) has ropelength `⊤`. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] L / thickness L

/-- The ropelength of the knot (or link) type of `L`: the infimum of the ropelength over all
subsets of `ℝ³` ambient isotopic to `L`. It is finite exactly when the type of `L` is tame. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (L' : Set ℝ³) (_ : IsAmbientIsotopic L L'), ropelength L'

/-- Orthogonal projection of `ℝ³` onto the plane of the first two coordinates. -/
def proj (p : ℝ³) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  (p 0, p 1)

/-- The multiple points of the projection of `K` to the plane: the points of the plane lying under
at least two distinct points of `K`. -/
def multiplePoints (K : Set ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {q | ∃ x ∈ K, ∃ y ∈ K, x ≠ y ∧ proj x = q ∧ proj y = q}

/-- `K` has a *regular projection with `n` crossings*: the projection of `K` to the plane has
exactly `n` multiple points, and each of them lies under exactly two points of `K`. -/
def HasDiagramWithCrossings (K : Set ℝ³) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (multiplePoints K).encard = n ∧ ∀ q ∈ multiplePoints K, (K ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard = 2

/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of `K`: the least number of crossings in a regular
projection of a knot ambient isotopic to `K`. (Rotations are ambient isotopies, so projecting to a
fixed plane suffices.) By convention it is `0` when no such projection exists. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ K', IsAmbientIsotopic K K' ∧ HasDiagramWithCrossings K' n}

/--
**Linear ropelength conjecture.**
The ropelength of a knot type is at most a constant times its crossing number: there is a constant
$C$ such that every nontrivial tame knot type $K$ satisfies
$$L(K) \le C \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K).$$
That is, $L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$, sharpening the known bound
$L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$ of Diao–Ernst–Por–Ziegler.
No knot family with super-linear dependence of ropelength on crossing number has been observed,
and the tight upper bound is conjectured to be linear.

The unknot is excluded since it has crossing number `0` and positive ropelength. Tame knot types
are exactly those of finite ropelength, since a knot type contains a $C^{1,1}$ curve if and only if
it is tame.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ K : Set ℝ³, IsKnot K → ¬ IsAmbientIsotopic K unknot → minRopelength K ≠ ⊤ →
      minRopelength K ≤ C * crossingNumber K := by
  sorry

/--
**Ropelength of the Borromean rings.**
The ropelength of the Borromean rings is conjectured to be $58.006$ (thickness measured as a
radius), the ropelength of the critical configuration of Cantarella–Fu–Kusner–Sullivan–Wrinkle,
which is built from arcs of circles and clasp curves in three perpendicular planes and is
conjectured to be the ropelength minimizer. Since $58.006$ is a rounded value, the statement is
that the minimal ropelength rounds to $58.006$, i.e. lies in $[58.0055, 58.0065]$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.ii :
    minRopelength borromeanRings ∈ Set.Icc 58.0055 58.0065 := by
  sorry

end RopelengthProblems

Knots are subsets of ℝ³ homeomorphic to `Circle`; knot/link types are ambient isotopy classes: a jointly continuous family H : [0,1] → Homeomorph ℝ³ ℝ³ with H 0 = id and H 1 '' A = B. Types are thus unoriented and components unordered, which does not affect ropelength or crossing number. Inverse joint continuity is not required (automatic on ℝ³ by invariance of domain).
Ropelength of a type is the infimum (⨅ in ℝ≥0∞) over the isotopy class rather than a minimum; CKS prove the minimum is attained for tame types, so this is equivalent.

Crossing number is defined as the least n such that some representative has a projection to the x₀x₁-plane with exactly n multiple points, each lying under exactly two points of the knot (Set.encard = 2 excludes triple points). Projecting to a fixed plane suffices since rotations are ambient isotopies. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ropelength problems

The *ropelength* of a curve $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C)/\tau(C)$, the
quotient of its length by its *thickness* $\tau(C)$, the radius of the largest embedded normal
tube around $C$. The ropelength of a knot or link type is the minimal ropelength over all
curves of that type.

Following Cantarella, Kusner and Sullivan (after Gonzalez and Maddocks), the thickness of a
set $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is the infimum of the circumradius $r(x, y, z)$ over all
triples of distinct points of $L$, where $r(x, y, z) = \infty$ for collinear triples. Every
curve of finite ropelength is $C^{1,1}$, so no regularity needs to be imposed on the curves
over which the infimum is taken.

Thickness is measured as a *radius* (the Hopf link has ropelength $8\pi$), as in
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan and in the Wikipedia article.

This file states two open problems from the Wikipedia article:

* the ropelength of a nontrivial knot is bounded by a constant multiple of its crossing number;
* the ropelength of the Borromean rings is $58.006$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* J. Cantarella, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*,
  Invent. Math. 150 (2002), [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
* J. Cantarella, J. H. G. Fu, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, N. C. Wrinkle, *Criticality for the
  Gehring link problem*, Geom. Topol. 10 (2006),
  [arXiv:math/0402212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402212)
* Y. Diao, C. Ernst, A. Por, U. Ziegler, *The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in terms of
  their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019)
* T. Ashton, J. Cantarella, M. Piatek, E. Rawdon, *Knot tightening by constrained gradient
  descent*, Exp. Math. 20 (2011), [arXiv:1002.1723](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.1723)
-/

open MeasureTheory Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry ContDiff ENNReal NNReal

namespace RopelengthProblems

/- ### Knots, links and ambient isotopy -/

/-- Two subsets `A`, `B` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' A = B`.
Knot and link types are ambient isotopy classes. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : unitInterval → (ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³),
    Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
      H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' A = B

@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (A : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id A⟩

/-- A subset of `ℝ³` is a *knot* if it is the image of a topological embedding of the circle. -/
def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ ∧ Set.range γ = K

/-- The round unit circle in the plane `z = 0`, a representative of the unknot. -/
def unknot : Set ℝ³ :=
  {p | p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ p 2 = 0}

/-- The standard configuration of the Borromean rings: three ellipses with semi-axes `2` and `1`
lying in the three coordinate planes, arranged cyclically so that the major axis of each is the
minor axis direction of the next. Explicitly: the ellipse $x^2/4 + y^2 = 1$ in the plane $z = 0$,
the ellipse $y^2/4 + z^2 = 1$ in the plane $x = 0$ and the ellipse $z^2/4 + x^2 = 1$ in the plane
$y = 0$. -/
def borromeanRings : Set ℝ³ :=
  {p | p 2 = 0 ∧ p 0 ^ 2 / 4 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1} ∪ {p | p 0 = 0 ∧ p 1 ^ 2 / 4 + p 2 ^ 2 = 1} ∪
    {p | p 1 = 0 ∧ p 2 ^ 2 / 4 + p 0 ^ 2 = 1}

/- ### Thickness and ropelength -/

/-- The *thickness* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³` (Gonzalez–Maddocks, Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan):
the infimum, over all triples of distinct points `x y z ∈ L`, of the radius of the circle
through `x`, `y`, `z`. Collinear triples have circumradius `∞` and hence do not contribute to
the infimum, so it suffices to range over affinely independent triples.

For a `C^{1,1}` link this is the radius of the largest embedded normal tube around `L`, and a
curve of positive thickness is automatically `C^{1,1}`. -/
noncomputable def thickness (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (x ∈ L) (y ∈ L) (z ∈ L) (h : AffineIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z]),
    ENNReal.ofReal (Affine.Simplex.circumradius (⟨![x, y, z], h⟩ : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2))

/-- The *ropelength* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³`: its length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure) divided
by its thickness. It is `∞` if `L` has zero thickness. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] L / thickness L

/-- The ropelength of the knot or link type of `L`: the infimum of the ropelength over all sets
ambient isotopic to `L`. For a tame link type this infimum is attained (Cantarella, Kusner,
Sullivan); for a wild one it is `∞`. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (L' : Set ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic L L'), ropelength L'

@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem minRopelength_le {L L' : Set ℝ³} (h : AmbientIsotopic L L') :
    minRopelength L ≤ ropelength L' :=
  iInf₂_le L' h

/- ### Crossing number -/

/-- Orthogonal projection of `ℝ³` onto the `xy`-plane. -/
def proj (x : ℝ³) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  (x 0, x 1)

/-- `γ : ℝ → ℝ³` is a *smooth knot parametrisation*: a smooth, `1`-periodic, regular curve
which is injective on a period. Its image is a smooth (in particular tame) knot. -/
structure IsSmoothKnotParam (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0

/-- The *crossings* of the projection of `γ` to the `xy`-plane: the points of the plane with at
least two preimages on the curve. -/
def crossings (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {q | 2 ≤ (Set.range γ ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard}

/-- The projection of `γ` to the `xy`-plane is *regular*: the projected curve is an immersion,
it has only finitely many multiple points, every multiple point is a double point (exactly two
preimages on the curve), and at every double point the two strands cross transversally. -/
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  immersion : ∀ t, proj (deriv γ t) ≠ 0
  finite : (crossings γ).Finite
  encard_le_two : ∀ q, (Set.range γ ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard ≤ 2
  transverse : ∀ s t, γ s ≠ γ t → proj (γ s) = proj (γ t) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![proj (deriv γ s), proj (deriv γ t)]

/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of `K`: the minimal number of crossings in a knot
diagram of `K`, i.e. in a regular projection to the `xy`-plane of a smooth knot ambient isotopic
to `K`. Every direction of projection is covered, since rotations are ambient isotopies. The
value is `⊤` if `K` has no smooth representative (e.g. for a wild knot). -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ))
    (_ : IsRegularProjection γ), (crossings γ).encard

@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem crossingNumber_le {K : Set ℝ³} {γ : ℝ → ℝ³} (hγ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ)
    (hK : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ)) (hp : IsRegularProjection γ) :
    crossingNumber K ≤ (crossings γ).encard :=
  iInf₂_le_of_le γ hγ <| iInf₂_le hK hp

/- ### The problems -/

/--
**Linear ropelength bound.** For every knot $K$ the ropelength $L(K)$ satisfies
$L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$ (Diao, Ernst, Por, Ziegler), and
there are knot families with $L(K) = \Theta(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$. No knot family with
super-linear dependence of ropelength on crossing number has been observed, and it is conjectured
that the tight upper bound is linear: there is a constant $c > 0$ such that
$L(K) \le c \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ for every nontrivial knot $K$.

The unknot has crossing number $0$ but positive ropelength ($2\pi$), so it must be excluded.
For a wild knot both the crossing number and the ropelength are infinite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ≥0, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : Set ℝ³, IsKnot K → ¬ AmbientIsotopic K unknot →
      minRopelength K ≤ c * (crossingNumber K : ℝ≥0∞) := by
  sorry

/--
**Ropelength of the Borromean rings.** The ropelength of the Borromean rings is conjectured to be
$58.006$ (Cantarella, Fu, Kusner, Sullivan, Wrinkle), the length of an explicit configuration
built from three planar "guitar-shaped" components made of parametrised arcs, in units where the
thickness is the radius of the tube. Since $58.006$ is a rounded figure, the statement asserts
that the ropelength agrees with $58.006$ to three decimal places, i.e. lies in
$[58.0055, 58.0065]$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.ii :
    minRopelength borromeanRings ∈ Set.Icc (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0055) (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0065) := by
  sorry

end RopelengthProblems

For slot (ii) I chose the rounding-tolerance reading [58.0055, 58.0065] (agreement with 58.006 to three decimal places) rather than the truncation interval [58.006, 58.007) suggested as an example in the notes, since the CFKSW value is only known to be ≈ 58.0060 and a rounding tolerance is the standard reading of a rounded figure.

/-!
# Ropelength problems

The *ropelength* of a knot or link $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is the quotient
$\operatorname{Len}(L) / \tau(L)$ of its length by its *thickness* $\tau(L)$, the radius of the
largest embedded normal tube around $L$. Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, the thickness is the infimum of the circumradii of all non-degenerate
triangles with vertices on $L$; it is positive exactly when $L$ is a $C^{1,1}$ embedded curve.
The ropelength of a knot or link *type* is the infimum of the ropelength over all curves of that
type. Minimisers exist and are called *tight* or *ideal* knots and links.

Ropelength is measured in units of the tube radius, so that the tight Hopf link (two round circles
of radius $2$ through each other's centres) has ropelength $8\pi$.

This file states two open problems about ropelength.

* **Linear dependence on the crossing number.** For every nontrivial knot $K$,
  $\operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4} \lesssim L(K) \lesssim \operatorname{Cr}(K)\log^5\operatorname{Cr}(K)$,
  where $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the crossing number. No knot family with super-linear growth of
  ropelength in the crossing number is known, and it is conjectured that the tight upper bound is
  linear: $L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$.
* **The Borromean rings.** Cantarella, Fu, Kusner, Sullivan and Wrinkle constructed a
  ropelength-critical configuration of the Borromean rings from parameterised arcs (each component
  is planar and guitar-shaped) with ropelength $\approx 58.0060$, and conjecture that it is tight.
  So the minimum ropelength of the Borromean rings is conjectured to be $58.006$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

  Invent. Math. 150 (2002), 257–286

  [Criticality for the Gehring link problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402212),
  Geom. Topol. 10 (2006), 2055–2116
* Y. Diao, C. Ernst, A. Por, U. Ziegler,
  [The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in terms of their crossing numbers](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218216519500858),
  J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019)
-/

namespace RopelengthProblems

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ContDiff ENNReal EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory

/- ### Links, ambient isotopy, thickness and ropelength -/

/-- Two subsets `A` and `B` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family of
homeomorphisms `h_t : ℝ³ → ℝ³`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, with `h_0 = id` and `h_1 '' A = B`.
Knots and links are considered up to this equivalence. -/
def IsAmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : C(ℝ³, ℝ³),
    Nonempty ((ContinuousMap.id ℝ³).HomotopyWith h fun f => IsHomeomorph f) ∧ h '' A = B

/-- Ambient isotopy is reflexive: the constant family of identity maps is an ambient isotopy. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem isAmbientIsotopic_refl (A : Set ℝ³) : IsAmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨ContinuousMap.id ℝ³, ⟨ContinuousMap.HomotopyWith.refl _ (Homeomorph.refl ℝ³).isHomeomorph⟩,
    image_id A⟩

/-- The *thickness* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³` (typically a knot or link): the infimum of the circumradii
of all non-degenerate triangles with vertices on `L`. For a link, this is the radius of the largest
embedded normal tube around `L`; it is positive exactly when `L` is a `C^{1,1}` curve. -/
noncomputable def thickness (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (T : Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ³) (_ : ∀ i, T.points i ∈ L), ENNReal.ofReal T.circumradius

/-- The *ropelength* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³` (typically a knot or link): its length, measured by the
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (for a link, the total length of its components), divided by its
thickness. A link of zero thickness has infinite ropelength. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] L / thickness L

/-- The minimum ropelength of the knot or link type of `L`: the infimum of the ropelength over all
sets ambient isotopic to `L`. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (L' : Set ℝ³) (_ : IsAmbientIsotopic L L'), ropelength L'

/- ### Smooth knots, regular projections and the crossing number -/

/-- `γ : ℝ → ℝ³` parametrises a *smooth knot*: it is `1`-periodic, smooth, has nowhere vanishing
derivative, and is injective on a period. Its image `range γ` is a tame knot. -/
structure IsSmoothKnot (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0
  injOn : InjOn γ (Ico 0 1)

/-- The round unit circle in the `xy`-plane, a representative of the unknot. -/
def unknot : Set ℝ³ := {x | x 2 = 0 ∧ x 0 ^ 2 + x 1 ^ 2 = 1}

/-- Orthogonal projection of `ℝ³` onto the `xy`-plane, identified with `ℝ × ℝ`. -/
def proj (x : ℝ³) : ℝ × ℝ := (x 0, x 1)

/-- The *crossings* of the `xy`-projection of a `1`-periodic closed curve `γ`: pairs of parameters
`s < t` in `[0, 1)` whose points have the same projection. -/
def crossings (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ p.2 ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ p.1 < p.2 ∧ proj (γ p.1) = proj (γ p.2)}

/-- The `xy`-projection of the `1`-periodic closed curve `γ` is *regular*: the projected curve
is an immersion, no point of the plane has three or more preimages, there are finitely many double
points, and at each double point the two strands cross transversally. -/
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  proj_deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, proj (deriv γ t) ≠ 0
  finite_crossings : (crossings γ).Finite
  no_triple_point : ∀ s ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ u ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1,
    s ≠ t → t ≠ u → s ≠ u → proj (γ s) = proj (γ t) → proj (γ t) ≠ proj (γ u)
  transverse : ∀ s ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, s ≠ t → proj (γ s) = proj (γ t) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![proj (deriv γ s), proj (deriv γ t)]

/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of `K`: the least number of crossings in a regular
projection of a smooth knot ambient isotopic to `K`. Since any direction of projection can be
realised by rotating the knot (an ambient isotopy), projecting to the `xy`-plane loses no
generality. A wild knot type has no such projection, and gets the junk value `0`. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ : ℝ → ℝ³, IsSmoothKnot γ ∧ IsRegularProjection γ ∧
    IsAmbientIsotopic (range γ) K ∧ (crossings γ).ncard = n}

/- ### The problems -/

/-- **Linear dependence of ropelength on the crossing number.**
There is a universal constant $c > 0$ such that every nontrivial knot $K$ satisfies
$L(K) \le c \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K)$, where $L(K)$ is the minimum ropelength of the knot type of
$K$ and $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is its crossing number; that is, $L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$.
This sharpens the proven bound $L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$;
no knot family with super-linear dependence of ropelength on the crossing number has been
observed. Tame knot types are represented by smooth knots `γ`, and the unknot, which has crossing
number $0$ but positive ropelength, is excluded. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ γ : ℝ → ℝ³, IsSmoothKnot γ → ¬ IsAmbientIsotopic (range γ) unknot →
      minRopelength (range γ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * crossingNumber (range γ)) := by
  sorry

/-- The `i`-th component of a standard configuration of the Borromean rings: an ellipse with
semi-axes `2` and `1` in a coordinate plane. Explicitly, the three components are
* `i = 0`: `{z = 0, x² / 4 + y² = 1}` (in the `xy`-plane, major axis along the `x`-axis),
* `i = 1`: `{x = 0, y² / 4 + z² = 1}` (in the `yz`-plane, major axis along the `y`-axis),
* `i = 2`: `{y = 0, z² / 4 + x² = 1}` (in the `zx`-plane, major axis along the `z`-axis). -/
def borromeanComponent (i : Fin 3) : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x | x (i + 2) = 0 ∧ x i ^ 2 / 4 + x (i + 1) ^ 2 = 1}

/-- A standard configuration of the **Borromean rings**: three mutually perpendicular ellipses
with semi-axes `2` and `1`, one in each coordinate plane, with their major axes arranged
cyclically, see `RopelengthProblems.borromeanComponent`. -/
def borromeanRings : Set ℝ³ := ⋃ i, borromeanComponent i

/-- The three components of `borromeanRings` are pairwise disjoint, so it is a link. -/
@[category test, AMS 53 57]
theorem pairwise_disjoint_borromeanComponent :
    Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (borromeanComponent i) (borromeanComponent j) := by
  intro i j hij
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  rintro x ⟨hi, hi'⟩ ⟨hj, hj'⟩
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp only [Fin.isValue, Fin.reduceAdd, Fin.zero_eta,
    Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, ne_eq, not_true_eq_false] at hij hi hi' hj hj' <;>
    rw [hi] at hj' <;> rw [hj] at hi' <;> nlinarith

/-- **Ropelength of the Borromean rings.**
The minimum ropelength of the Borromean rings, measured in units of the tube radius, is
conjectured to be $58.006$ (that is, it rounds to $58.006$ at three decimal places). The
conjectured minimiser is the ropelength-critical configuration of Cantarella, Fu, Kusner, Sullivan
and Wrinkle, built from parameterised arcs into three planar guitar-shaped components, whose
ropelength is approximately $58.0060$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.ii :
    minRopelength borromeanRings ∈ Ico (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0055) (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0065) := by
  sorry

end RopelengthProblems

The ropelength of a knot/link type is the ⨅ over all sets ambient isotopic to the given set of their ropelength (CKS definition); this automatically ranges over exactly the C^{1,1} embeddings of the type since all others have infinite ropelength.

/-!
# Ropelength problems

Ropelength is length divided by the radius of the largest embedded normal tube. This file records
conjectures about its growth with crossing number and its value for the Borromean rings.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Cantarella, Kusner and Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- [Ashton, Cantarella, Piatek and Rawdon, *Knot Tightening by Constrained Gradient Descent*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.1723)
-/

open Set MeasureTheory Topology
open scoped ENNReal

namespace RopelengthProblems

abbrev Point3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
abbrev Point2 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- Two subsets of space have the same link type if an ambient isotopy takes one to the other.
Joint continuity is required both for the family of homeomorphisms and for its inverses. -/
def SameLinkType (K L : Set Point3) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → (Point3 ≃ₜ Point3),
    F ⟨0, by simp⟩ = Homeomorph.refl Point3 ∧
    Continuous (fun p : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Point3 ↦ F p.1 p.2) ∧
    Continuous (fun p : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Point3 ↦ (F p.1).symm p.2) ∧
    F ⟨1, by simp⟩ '' K = L

/-- The carrier of a closed polygonal curve. The vertices are indexed cyclically by `Fin (n + 1)`.-/
def polygonCarrier {n : ℕ} (v : Fin (n + 1) → Point3) : Set Point3 :=
  ⋃ i, segment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1))

/-- A polygonal knot is a simple cyclic polygon whose carrier is topologically embedded. -/
def IsPolygonalKnot {n : ℕ} (v : Fin (n + 1) → Point3) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective v ∧
  (∀ i j, i ≠ j →
    Disjoint (openSegment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1))) (openSegment ℝ (v j) (v (j + 1)))) ∧
  ∃ f : Circle → Point3, IsEmbedding f ∧ range f = polygonCarrier v

/-- A set is a tame knot if it has an embedded polygonal representative in its ambient isotopy
class. -/
def IsTameKnot (K : Set Point3) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin (n + 1) → Point3), IsPolygonalKnot v ∧ SameLinkType K (polygonCarrier v)

/-- The standard planar unknot. -/
def standardUnknot : Set Point3 :=
  {p | p 2 = 0 ∧ p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1}

/-- A tame knot is nontrivial when it is not ambient-equivalent to the standard unknot. -/
def IsNontrivialKnot (K : Set Point3) : Prop :=
  IsTameKnot K ∧ ¬ SameLinkType K standardUnknot

/-- The two cyclic edges with initial vertices `i` and `j` have no common endpoint. -/
def nonAdjacentEdges {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin (n + 1)) : Prop :=
  Disjoint ({i, i + 1} : Finset (Fin (n + 1))) {j, j + 1}

/-- Two polygon edges cross in the interior after applying the planar projection `q`. -/
def projectedEdgesCross {n : ℕ} (v : Fin (n + 1) → Point3)
    (q : Point3 →ₗ[ℝ] Point2) (i j : Fin (n + 1)) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ openSegment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1)), ∃ b ∈ openSegment ℝ (v j) (v (j + 1)), q a = q b

/-- A projection of a polygonal knot is regular if vertices project away from nonincident edge
interiors, every projected edge is nondegenerate, crossings are transverse, and no three edge
interiors meet at one projected point. -/
def IsRegularProjection {n : ℕ} (v : Fin (n + 1) → Point3)
    (q : Point3 →ₗ[ℝ] Point2) : Prop :=
  Function.Surjective q ∧
  (∀ i, q (v (i + 1) - v i) ≠ 0) ∧
  (∀ i j, i ≠ j → projectedEdgesCross v q i j →
    ¬ ∃ r : ℝ, q (v (j + 1) - v j) = r • q (v (i + 1) - v i)) ∧
  (∀ i j, nonAdjacentEdges i j →
    q (v i) ∉ openSegment ℝ (q (v j)) (q (v (j + 1)))) ∧
  (∀ i j k, i ≠ j → i ≠ k → j ≠ k →
    ¬ ∃ a ∈ openSegment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1)),
      ∃ b ∈ openSegment ℝ (v j) (v (j + 1)),
      ∃ c ∈ openSegment ℝ (v k) (v (k + 1)), q a = q b ∧ q a = q c)

/-- The number of crossings in a regular polygonal projection. -/
noncomputable def projectionCrossingCount {n : ℕ} (v : Fin (n + 1) → Point3)
    (q : Point3 →ₗ[ℝ] Point2) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact ((Finset.univ ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter fun (ij : Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1)) =>
    nonAdjacentEdges ij.1 ij.2 ∧ ij.1 < ij.2 ∧ projectedEdgesCross v q ij.1 ij.2).card

/-- The crossing number of a tame knot: the least number of crossings in a regular polygonal
diagram of its knot type. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set Point3) : ℕ :=
  sInf {c | ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin (n + 1) → Point3) (q : Point3 →ₗ[ℝ] Point2),
    IsPolygonalKnot v ∧ SameLinkType K (polygonCarrier v) ∧ IsRegularProjection v q ∧
      projectionCrossingCount v q = c}

/-- The reach (radius thickness) of a subset of Euclidean space: the largest radius below which
every point has a unique nearest point in the subset. -/
noncomputable def thickness (K : Set Point3) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup {r | ∀ x : Point3, Metric.infEDist x K < r →
    ∃! y : Point3, y ∈ K ∧ edist x y = Metric.infEDist x K}

/-- Ropelength of a positive-thickness curve, using one-dimensional Hausdorff measure for total
length and radius (rather than diameter) thickness. -/
noncomputable def ropelengthOf (K : Set Point3) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] K / thickness K

/-- Minimum ropelength in the ambient link type of `K`. Restricting to positive reach is the
set-based version of taking the infimum over embedded `C^{1,1}` representatives. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (K : Set Point3) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ L : Set Point3, SameLinkType K L ∧ 0 < thickness L ∧ ropelengthOf L = r}

/-- A standard three-ellipse representative of the Borromean rings. -/
def borromeanRings : Set Point3 :=
  {p | p 0 = 0 ∧ p 1 ^ 2 + (p 2 / 2) ^ 2 = 1} ∪
  {p | p 1 = 0 ∧ (p 0 / 2) ^ 2 + p 2 ^ 2 = 1} ∪
  {p | p 2 = 0 ∧ p 0 ^ 2 + (p 1 / 2) ^ 2 = 1}

namespace ropelength_problems.parts

/-- It is conjectured that the tight upper bound for ropelength is linear in crossing number:
there is a universal constant $c>0$ such that every nontrivial tame knot $K$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) \le c\,\operatorname{Cr}(K)$. The unknot is excluded because its crossing
number is zero while its ropelength is positive. -/
@[category research open, AMS 57]
theorem i : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : Set Point3, IsNontrivialKnot K →
    ropelength K ≤ ENNReal.ofReal c * crossingNumber K := by
  sorry

/-- In radius-thickness units, the minimum total ropelength of the three components of the
Borromean rings is conjectured to round to $58.006$. Concretely, it is conjectured to lie in the
half-open rounding interval $[58.006,58.007)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 57]
theorem ii : (58.006 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ropelength borromeanRings ∧
    ropelength borromeanRings < 58.007 := by
  sorry

end ropelength_problems.parts

end RopelengthProblems
modeling_decisions: Modeled knot/link type by an explicit ambient isotopy: a jointly continuous family of homeomorphisms starting at the identity, with jointly continuous inverses.

Modeled tame knots as subsets ambient-isotopic to the carrier of a simple cyclic polygon. This makes the quantification in part (i) range over nontrivial tame knot types and excludes the unknot topologically.

Defined classical crossing number as the minimum crossing count over regular planar linear projections of simple polygonal representatives in the same ambient-isotopy type. Regularity excludes degenerate edges, vertex-edge coincidences, tangencies, overlaps, and triple crossings.

Used Federer reach as radius thickness: the supremum of radii for which every point closer than that radius has a unique nearest point on the curve. Positive reach is the set-based formulation of the intended embedded C^{1,1} representatives.

Defined curve/link length by one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, so a disconnected link's length is the total length of all components, and defined knot/link ropelength as the infimum of length divided by radius thickness over positive-reach representatives in the ambient type.
Quantified the linear-bound constant in ℝ and coerced it with ENNReal.ofReal, preventing the vacuous choice c = ∞.

Represented the Borromean rings by the standard cyclic arrangement of three pairwise-disjoint perpendicular ellipses, with alternating major axes, and took the ropelength invariant of its ambient-isotopy type.
Interpreted the rounded value 58.006 using the decomposition table's suggested half-open interval [58.006, 58.007), rather than asserting exact equality to a rounded decimal.

modeling_decisions: For slot (i), the intended statement is the multiplicative uniform bound ∃ c > 0, ∀ nontrivial tame knots K, ropelength K ≤ c * crossingNumber K; the nontrivial restriction is needed because the unknot has crossing number zero and positive ropelength.

For slot (ii), the decimal 58.006 is rounded, so a faithful eventual formalization should use the stated unit-radius convention and a rounding interval such as 58.006 ≤ ropelength BorromeanRings ∧ ropelength BorromeanRings < 58.007, unless the exact parameterized CFKSW candidate configuration and its minimizer claim are formalized instead.

ropelength_problems.parts.i.why: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no geometric knot type (or tame-knot predicate), ambient isotopy relation, knot crossing number, or ropelength/thickness invariant. Mathlib's IsEmbedding, EuclideanSpace, and eVariationOn are insufficient: faithfully stating this slot requires taking the infimum of length/thickness over C^{1,1} representatives of one ambient-isotopy class and comparing it with the minimum number of crossings in regular planar diagrams. Introducing arbitrary functions called ropelength and crossingNumber would be a placeholder, while defining this missing reusable knot-theory and geometric-measure-theory foundation in the conjecture file cannot be done faithfully without substantial new library development.

ropelength_problems.parts.ii.why: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no link type, ambient isotopy relation, canonical Borromean-rings link type, or link ropelength/thickness invariant. A faithful statement needs total component length divided by thickness, minimized over C^{1,1} embeddings ambient-isotopic to the Borromean rings. Naming an unconstrained object 'Borromean rings' or using only the property that every two-component sublink is trivial would not identify the Borromean link type faithfully.
